'''Liqun Luo''' ({{zh|s=骆利群}}; born January 1966) is a neuroscientist in the Department of Biology at [[Stanford University]], where he is the Ann and Bill Swindells Professor in the School of Humanities and Sciences,<ref name=Stanford>{{cite web|url=https://profiles.stanford.edu/liqun-luo|title=Liqun Luo's Profile - Stanford Profiles|website=profiles.stanford.edu}}</ref> and an investigator of the [[Howard Hughes Medical Institute]].<ref name=HHMI>{{cite web|url=https://www.hhmi.org/scientists/liqun-luo|title=Liqun Luo, PhD - HHMI.org}}</ref> His laboratory studies the development and organization of neural circuits,<ref name=Stanford /> and he is the author of the textbook ''Principles of Neurobiology''.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Book review|journal=Cell|date=8 October 2015 |volume=163 |issue=2 |pages=267–268 |doi=10.1016/j.cell.2015.09.039 |last1=Li |first1=Yulong |last2=Rao |first2=Yi |s2cid=46666796 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Luo was born in January 1966 in [[Shanghai]], China. After graduating from the middle school of [[No.1 High School Affiliated to East China Normal University]], he was admitted to the [[Special Class for the Gifted Young]] at the [[University of Science and Technology of China]] (USTC) in 1981 and skipped high school.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ustcif.org/default.php/content/258/|title=818 骆利群|date=2008-01-16|website=University of Science and Technology of China Initiative Foundation|language=zh-Hans|access-date=2018-10-14}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://bio.pku.edu.cn/displaynews2.php?id=6725|title=从科大少年班到Stanford教授：主观报告和客观分析|date=2008-06-12|website=Peking University|access-date=2018-10-14}}</ref>

Luo earned his bachelor's degree in molecular biology from the [[University of Science and Technology of China]] in 1986.<ref name="Stanford" /> He completed his PhD at [[Brandeis University]] in 1992, studying the ''[[Drosophila melanogaster]]'' homolog of the [[Amyloid precursor protein]].<ref name="CurrentBiology">{{cite journal|title=Liqun Luo|first=Liqun|last=Luo|date=1 September 2008|journal=Current Biology|volume=18|issue=18|pages=R842–R843|doi=10.1016/j.cub.2008.07.005|s2cid=27180157|doi-access=free|bibcode=2008CBio...18.R842L }}</ref> After his postdoctoral work in the lab of [[Lily Jan]] and [[Yuh Nung Jan]] at the [[University of California in San Francisco]], he became an assistant professor in the Department of Biology at Stanford University in 1996.<ref name="CurrentBiology" />

== Research ==
Luo's research focuses on the assembly and organization of neural circuits.<ref name=CurrentBiology /> His lab has invented tools to facilitate [[Mosaic (genetics)|mosaic]] analysis in flies ([[MARCM]]) and mice (MADM).<ref name = Q&A>{{cite journal|title=Liqun Luo|date=1 August 2016|journal=Neuron|volume=91|issue=3|pages=508–510|doi=10.1016/j.neuron.2016.07.017|doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
Luo has been an Investigator of the Howard Hughes Medical Institute since 2005,<ref name=HHMI /> and is a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/liqun-luo-vaqww8/|title=Liqun Luo|website=www.nasonline.org}}</ref> and the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.amacad.org/content/system/search.aspx?t=50&s=liqun+luo|title=Academy of Arts & Sciences Website Search|website=www.amacad.org}}</ref> He has received numerous awards including the Technology Innovation in Neuroscience award from the [[McKnight Foundation]] and The Young Investigator Award from the [[Society for Neuroscience]].<ref name=Stanford />
